rules.statement: A browser OAuth/OpenID Connect client or flow explorer offers only the authorization-code flow with PKCE `S256`; implicit, hybrid front-channel-token and resource-owner password flows must not be selectable.
rules.why: A tool that can emit implicit, hybrid or password flows normalizes insecure patterns and contradicts the OAuth 2.1 / RFC 9700 security-practice default.
rules.check: Look for response_type values containing `token` or `id_token` without `code`, `grant_type=password`, PKCE `plain`, or UI options that let a user pick those flows.

rules.statement: A frontend app gets its OAuth client id from the run-time bootstrap endpoint, never from a build-time value such as an environment variable baked into the bundle.
rules.why: The client id is a deployment coordinate; a build-time value breaks the 'one bundle, every tier' invariant.
rules.check: Look for client ids read from `import.meta.env`, `process.env`, Vite `define` constants or hard-coded literals in frontend app code.

rules.statement: Keep protocol flow orchestration and audit or classification logic in UI-free, framework-free modules with their own unit tests, and compose them from the shared auth primitives rather than embedding them in components.
rules.why: Pure, unit-tested logic makes a status or flow change a signal rather than noise and keeps the logic reusable outside the UI.
rules.check: Look for PKCE, token-exchange, discovery-audit or classification logic written inside UI components, or new logic modules added without accompanying unit tests.
